title: A Trail for the Rivergate
premise: Ulyana Okonkwo, a railroad engineer who keeps a stolen map of closed lines as her only inheritance, arrives in the tidal town of Rivergate just as an ebb tide exposes a cave mouth the locals have charged tourists to glimpse for a century. Inside lies the Meridian Star, a wrecked salvage ship whose manifest could prove her grandfather was framed for the disaster that ruined his railway — and whose salvage rights the corrupt Harrow fleet means to claim first. Racing the six tides before the cave seals again, Ulyana allies with Tomas, a diver bound by duty to the very fleet she's outrunning, and the two fall in love across the widening gap between their loyalties. In the end, she wins the wreck but loses the legal claim, so she chooses justice outside the law: publishing the manifest and the closed-line map to every town the railway abandoned, then walking the open line out of Rivergate with Tomas beside her.
about_author: Hazel Joubert is a former coastal surveyor who spent a decade mapping tide lines along drowned railways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about women who measure the world in distances they can't afford to stop crossing.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On a night freight through the marsh country, she studies her grandfather's hand-inked map of abandoned rail lines, deciding which dying town to surface in next. Emotional beat: rootless competence — she's skilled everywhere, welcome nowhere.

chapters.title: Arrival at Rivergate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She steps off at Rivergate, a town built on salvage money and salt rot, and takes a room above a chandlery. The Harrow fleet's cranes dominate the harbor. Emotional beat: wary observation, the instinct to catalog exits.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. An unprecedented ebb drains the bay farther than any almanac predicts, and the sea floor opens into a cave mouth locals call the Tollgate. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the whole town turns to stare at her, the stranger.

chapters.title: Admission to a Legend
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The cave's keeper, old Mrs. Vann, charges Ulyana a coin and a warning: everyone who enters owes the sea something. Inside, Ulyana glimpses iron ribs and a nameplate — Meridian Star. Emotional beat: recognition; her grandfather's handwriting is on the hull.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She works out the tidal math: the cave seals in six tides, and the wreck sits in a flooded chamber reachable only at low slack. She has a window, not a plan. Emotional beat: cold clarity of the engineer — the sea keeps a schedule.

chapters.title: The Harrow Claim
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Diver Tomas Reinhart briefs the Harrow fleet on the cave, concealing that he's already seen a second entrance. His contract binds him; his conscience doesn't. Emotional beat: the first crack in a dutiful life.

chapters.title: A Diver on the Platform
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tomas catches her surveying the cave and, instead of reporting her, corrects her tide tables. Neither trusts the other; both need what the other knows. Emotional beat: reluctant respect.

chapters.title: What the Grandfather Buried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the chandlery's ledgers she finds the Meridian Star was hauling evidence against the railway syndicate when it 'sank' — the same syndicate that framed her grandfather and closed his lines. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Mouth
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas shows Ulyana the inland entrance through a collapsed rail tunnel — a line on her grandfather's map he never marked. Emotional beat: the map and the man begin to agree, and it unsettles her.

chapters.title: Contract of Salt
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Fleet boss Adelene Harrow locks the divers into a salvage contract with a penalty clause: anyone who aids an outsider forfeits everything, including diving rights for life. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a weight belt.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana and Tomas enter the tunnel at low slack, swimming the flooded gallery to the wreck's cargo hold. She finds a sealed strongbox stamped with her family's initials. Emotional beat: terror and homecoming in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Strongbox Holds
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The box contains a manifest and a confession naming the syndicate — but the paper is waterlogged and will disintegrate unless preserved. Emotional beat: hope with a countdown on it.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Price
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vann's POV. The old keeper recognizes the Okonkwo name and reveals she helped hide the strongbox fifty years ago, paying for it with her son, lost to the cave. Emotional beat: inherited guilt, freely offered.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Adelene Harrow offers Ulyana a share and a safe exit if she surrenders the strongbox — and lets the fleet's version of history stand. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana refuses, and Harrow posts watchers on both cave mouths, turning the tide itself into a siege. Emotional beat: the cost of stopping, made literal.

chapters.title: Night Survey
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas secretly re-surveys the flooded chamber and finds the hull is failing — the wreck may collapse before the sixth tide. Emotional beat: a professional's dread he can't report to his employer.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Rivergate's townsfolk, whose grandfathers were paid off after the wreck, debate in the tavern: take Harrow's salvage money, or back the stranger. Emotional beat: a community remembering what it sold.

chapters.title: Barnacle and Bone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Second dive: Ulyana frees the manifest from the hold as the hull groans and a bulkhead lets go behind them. Tomas saves her from a collapsing spar. Emotional beat: gratitude she can't file under professional.

chapters.title: The Space Between Tides
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Stranded in an air pocket waiting for slack water, Ulyana and Tomas talk — her map, his contract, the lives they've each deferred. Emotional beat: love arriving in the one place neither can leave.

chapters.title: Surfacing Changed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They surface at dawn, and a Harrow watcher sees them together. Tomas must choose what to tell Adelene. Emotional beat: the first lie to the duty that raised him.

chapters.title: Preservation and Perjury
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Mrs. Vann helps preserve the manifest with chandlery wax and alcohol, but a page — the one naming the syndicate's living chairman — is missing, torn out long ago. Emotional beat: proof that proves almost enough.

chapters.title: The Chairman's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana identifies the missing page's likely thief: the cave's former keeper, Mrs. Vann's late husband, who sold out decades ago. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations, and forgiveness offered anyway.

chapters.title: Harrow Moves Early
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Adelene, tipped off, orders the fleet to blast the inland tunnel open and take the wreck by force — collapsing the chamber and the evidence with it. Emotional beat: Tomas realizing his employer would rather bury the truth than salvage it.

chapters.title: Sabotage of the Good Kind
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas fakes an equipment failure to delay the blasting, burning his last shred of cover. Emotional beat: the moment duty inverts — he now serves the wreck, not the fleet.

chapters.title: Wanted in Rivergate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Harrow accuses Ulyana of sabotage and theft; the magistrate, on Harrow's payroll, issues a warrant. The town shelters her but can't stop the law. Emotional beat: hunted in the first town that felt like shelter.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Standoff
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Fleet crews and townsfolk face off at the tunnel mouth; Mrs. Vann stands on the tracks her husband's silence helped abandon. Emotional beat: the town finally paying its old debt.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With the tunnel half-blasted, the dive window shrinks. Ulyana and Tomas plan one last descent to recover the ship's log — the page that names the chairman — from the captain's safe. Emotional beat: exhaustion transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Captain's Safe
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Third and deepest dive. In the flooded wheelhouse, Ulyana cracks the safe and finds the log — and her grandfather's final letter, written the night he was framed. Emotional beat: a conversation across fifty years of water.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The hull gives way as they exit; Tomas is pinned by a falling plate while Ulyana, log in hand, is dragged toward the surface by the turning tide. Emotional beat: the map of her life tearing in half.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide, One Diver
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Against every instinct, Ulyana goes back down on the fifth tide alone and frees Tomas with a rail jack from her survey kit. Emotional beat: love against duty — she chooses the man over the evidence, and carries out both anyway.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vann's POV. Mrs. Vann produces her husband's hidden half-page, kept fifty years out of shame, and gives it to Ulyana. Emotional beat: a town's conscience, paid in full at last.

chapters.title: Harrow's Last Tide
chapters.summary: Adelene's POV. Adelene, facing ruin if the manifest goes public, offers Ulyana everything — the fleet, the claim, a name — to burn it. Emotional beat: the villain's own inheritance of duty, and her refusal to break it.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide Begins
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The cave starts sealing. Harrow's crew makes a final rush through the tunnel; the townsfolk flood the tracks with a decommissioned locomotive from the closed-line map. Emotional beat: the abandoned railway, weaponized for justice.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The cave closes with Harrow's foremen trapped outside the chamber and the evidence safe in Ulyana's hands. Mrs. Vann's son's watch, recovered from the wreck, is laid to rest on the tide line. Emotional beat: grief given a grave.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Court
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The magistrate moves to seize the manifest as 'salvage evidence'; Ulyana reads her grandfather's letter aloud in court, naming the chairman. Emotional beat: the law as a door that only opens from the inside.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Before the court can bury the file, Ulyana and Tomas print the manifest, log, and closed-line map on the chandlery press and nail copies to every door in Rivergate — and mail them to every town on the map. Emotional beat: the truth, made unownable.

chapters.title: The Fleet Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Divers walk out of the Harrow fleet; Adelene, abandoned, signs over the wreck's historical rights rather than face her own crews. Tomas surrenders his contract and his livelihood in the same signature. Emotional beat: freedom that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The Chairman Falls
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. News arrives: the syndicate chairman, exposed by a hundred mailed copies, is arrested as investors flee. Her grandfather's lines are ordered reopened. Emotional beat: vindication that arrives too late to matter more than the people beside her.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana walks the first reopened line out of Rivergate, adding new towns to her grandfather's map in her own hand. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed and rewritten.

chapters.title: The Next Ebb
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomas, dual POV. On the open line, they plan the survey of the next closed route, the sea at their backs keeping its own schedule. Emotional beat: not an ending but a heading — two people who stopped moving alone.
